extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on request body — Arbitrary code execution via crafted pickle payload [verified: pickle.loads is called on raw request body/GET bytes with no allowlist or signature check; the token gate only authenticates the caller, it does not restrict payload content, so a crafted pickle achieves RCE.]

Unsafe eval() of user-controlled expression — Arbitrary code execution by escaping the fake sandbox [verified: eval() is called on a user-supplied expr string with only __builtins__ stripped from globals, a well-known bypassable sandboxing pattern (e.g. via object subclass introspection); no other validation of expr exists.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 template built from user input — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox-escape payloads embedded in the fragment parameter [verified: fragment is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string before render(), with no autoescaping/sandboxing of the template source itself, enabling classic SSTI/RCE via Jinja2 payloads.]

Path traversal with attacker-controlled file content leading to arbitrary file overwrite — Attacker can overwrite arbitrary files anywhere the process can write, including web-served or executable paths, potentially leading to RCE [verified: name and the full request body are both attacker-controlled and passed unsanitized to write_bytes; the internal-token gate authenticates the caller but performs no path or content validation, so arbitrary file overwrite (including outside private_exports) is reachable.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — If deployed without SECRET_KEY set, an attacker who knows this default (visible in any repo checkout) can forge session cookies, password-reset tokens, and CSRF tokens [verified: SECRET_KEY hardcoded fallback is present in source and used unless SECRET_KEY env var is set, enabling session/CSRF/password-reset token forgery if deployed with defaults.]

Hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY — Attacker can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens, leading to full account takeover if the app is deployed without overriding SECRET_KEY. [verified: Duplicate of idx 0 — same hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback confirmed present and reachable in deployment.]

Manager can download HR-restricted employee documents — A manager can read confidential HR/payroll documents about a direct report that were never marked visible to non-HR roles (e.g. disciplinary records, tax forms, medical documentation) [verified: The manager branch at documents/views.py:84 grants access based solely on doc.employee.manager_id matching, with no check on doc.category or visible_to_employee, unlike the employee's own-document branch (line 82) which requires visible_to_employee=True.]

CSV import mass-assigns arbitrary role and falls back to hardcoded weak default password — Any account created via bulk import without an explicit strong password gets 'changeme123', a well-known default; combined with unrestricted 'role' assignment from the CSV, this allows creation of hr_admin accounts with guessable credentials, leading to full account/privilege compromise if such rows are ever processed (e.g. a CSV built from an external template or shared by a less-trusted party). [verified: Combines confirmed mass-assignment of role and hardcoded default password in the same call, both real and unmitigated — most severe framing of the same underlying bug as idx 0/1/2/3.]

Path traversal via 'ref' parameter leading to arbitrary file write — Attacker can write attacker-influenced JSON containing SSN/card data to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the intended export directory [verified: ref is taken directly from GET with no sanitization and concatenated into a path under BASE_EXPORT_DIR before write_text; the only control is the shared internal-token header check, which authenticates the caller but does not validate the ref value, so a caller with the token can still traverse via '../'.]

CORS misconfiguration reflecting arbitrary Origin with credentials allowed — Any external site can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read responses containing sensitive payroll data [verified: The Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is hardcoded true, letting any origin make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response.]

NoSQL injection via unrestricted Mongo query filter — Data exfiltration or query-operator abuse (e.g. $where) against the backing datastore [verified: payload['filter'] (or the whole payload) is passed straight into MongoClient.find_one with no schema/operator validation, allowing injection of arbitrary query operators against the datastore.]

DEBUG defaults to True in production settings — Unhandled exceptions leak source code, local variables, SECRET_KEY presence, DB config, and other sensitive internals to unauthenticated attackers [verified: DEBUG defaults to True with no override, so any deployment missing the env var serves verbose stack traces and internals to unauthenticated visitors.]

Insecure DEBUG default (fail-open) — If deployed without explicitly setting DEBUG=False, Django exposes detailed stack traces, source code, settings values (including SECRET_KEY when combined with certain debug pages), and internal paths to any visitor. [verified: Duplicate of idx 1 — DEBUG fail-open default confirmed.]

Hardcoded fallback database password — An attacker aware of this default (from source access) could gain direct database access to all employee PII and payroll data if the DB is reachable and the env var was not set [verified: DB_PASSWORD hardcoded fallback 'hrpayroll123' is used whenever the env var is unset, a known weak credential granting DB access if network-reachable.]

Hardcoded weak default database password — If deployed without overriding DB_PASSWORD, the Postgres database (containing PII, salary data, password hashes) is protected only by a well-known weak credential, easily brute-forced or guessed by an attacker with network access to the DB port. [verified: Duplicate of idx 2 — hardcoded weak DB password fallback confirmed present.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints — Enables credential brute-forcing, password-reset token guessing, and automated account creation/spam [verified: No throttling, CAPTCHA, or lockout exists on register(), login, or password_reset views/urls, permitting unlimited brute-force or account-creation attempts.]

Self-approval of compensation change requests (missing separation of duties) — A manager can unilaterally push through a favorable salary/bonus change for a direct report (including collusive or fraudulent adjustments) without independent managerial review, weakening the intended dual-approval control before HR sign-off. [verified: comp_request_manager_approve (compensation/views.py:117-139) checks only role and manager-of-employee, never comp.requester != request.user, so the manager who authored and submitted the request can also perform the manager-approval step themselves, bypassing intended dual control before HR sign-off.]

Managers can view HR-confidential documents flagged not-visible-to-employee — A manager can read confidential HR documents attached to their direct reports (e.g. disciplinary notes, investigation records, or other files HR intentionally hid from the employee) that were never meant to be manager-visible either, exposing sensitive PII/HR data beyond the intended access scope. [verified: employee_detail only filters out visible_to_employee=False documents when request.user.role == ROLE_EMPLOYEE (line 170); a manager viewing a direct report via _can_view_employee gets the full unfiltered HRDocument queryset including HR-confidential records.]

Hardcoded default password assigned during CSV employee import — Accounts created via bulk import without an explicit password get a well-known default password enabling account takeover [verified: Duplicate report of the same hardcoded 'changeme123' fallback at line 310; confirmed present and unmitigated.]

Hardcoded weak default password for imported accounts — Newly imported accounts (potentially including elevated roles per the mass-assignment finding) are protected only by a well-known, guessable password until manually changed, enabling account takeover [verified: Same hardcoded default password issue as idx 1; no forced password-change flag exists on EmployeeProfile/User models.]

CSV export vulnerable to formula injection (CSV injection) — An employee who sets their own first/last name (via employee_edit, which any user can do for themselves) to a value beginning with '=', '+', '-rel', or '@' can inject a spreadsheet formula. When an HR admin opens the exported payroll/onboarding/policy CSV in Excel/Sheets, the formula executes, enabling data exfiltration to a remote server or arbitrary command execution via known Excel formula-inje [verified: export_center writes user-controlled fields like get_full_name() (settable via employee_edit self-edit) into CSV via csv.writer with no leading-character escaping for '=','+','-','@', a genuine CSV/formula injection risk when opened by HR admins.]

Open redirect via unvalidated 'lane' parameter — Phishing by crafting links that appear to originate from the trusted application domain [verified: next_url from the 'lane' GET param is passed directly to redirect() with no host/path allowlist, enabling open redirect to attacker-controlled destinations.]

TLS certificate verification disabled on outbound HTTPS request — Man-in-the-middle attacker can intercept or tamper with outbound integration traffic [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables certificate validation for the outbound urlopen call to the partner endpoint, a genuine missing-control TLS misconfiguration regardless of the fixed URL.]

Missing audience authorization check on policy detail view — Any authenticated employee (lowest-privilege role) can read the full content of HR-only or manager-only policies by ID, exposing internal HR/management policy content that should be restricted by audience tier. [verified: Confirmed: no role/audience check exists in policy_detail, unlike the filtering applied in policy_list.]

IDOR on policy detail view bypassing audience restriction — Any authenticated user can view restricted manager/HR-only policy content by guessing or incrementing the policy pk [verified: Same code path; get_object_or_404 with no audience check lets any authenticated user view restricted policies by pk.]

Account enumeration via registration error messages — Attacker can enumerate valid employee usernames and email addresses in the HR system, aiding targeted phishing or credential-stuffing attacks [verified: register() at accounts/views.py:31-34 returns distinct 'Username already taken.' vs 'Email already registered.' messages with no rate limiting, allowing enumeration of valid usernames/emails.]

Unvalidated employment_status value settable by managers — A manager can set an employee's employment_status to an arbitrary string not in the defined choices, which is used elsewhere (e.g. payroll_dashboard, _employee_qs_for_user) as an access/visibility gate — this could be leveraged to hide/reveal payroll or comp data in unintended ways or corrupt reporting relied on by HR/payroll workflows. [verified: employee_edit applies request.POST.get('employment_status', ...) with only a blanket strip, no validation against EmployeeProfile.STATUS_* choices, and _can_edit_employee permits self-edit for regular employees, so any user can set their own status to an arbitrary string used elsewhere as a visibility gate.]

CSV formula injection in onboarding export — Formula execution in the HR admin's spreadsheet application when opening the exported file, potentially leading to data exfiltration or code execution via malicious formulas (e.g. DDE) [verified: task.title and get_full_name() are user-editable and written via csv.writer with no leading-character sanitization, reaching an HR admin's spreadsheet app on open.]

CSV formula injection in policy acknowledgement export — Formula execution in the HR admin's spreadsheet application when opening the exported file, potentially leading to data exfiltration or code execution via malicious formulas [verified: ack.employee.user.get_full_name() (and policy.title) are written unsanitized to CSV, same unescaped pattern as the other export branches.]

Unvalidated assigned_to user id in HR request status update — An HR admin or manager can assign HR requests (which may reference sensitive payroll/benefits topics) to arbitrary user accounts, causing unintended notification/visibility change and breaking the intended assignment workflow; combined with any future feature that grants request-detail access to assignees, this could become a full IDOR data-exposure path. [verified: assigned_to_id is taken directly from POST with no check that the target user is a manager/HR admin or otherwise eligible, only the requester's role/ownership is validated; impact is limited to misdirected assignment/notification since no data exposure currently flows from assigned_to.]
